sections.h2: Who bills a house in the City of Homestead
sections.html:
Homestead sits inside Miami-Dade County, so the county Office of the Tax Collector, 200 NW 2nd Avenue in Miami, handles your bill. Its number is 305-375-5448. The city sets its own rate, as do the School Board and other districts, but none of them mails or collects the bill.

Value and exemption rulings come from the Property Appraiser, whose homestead line is 305-375-4712. The Clerk of Courts and Comptroller runs tax deed sales.

The name trips people up. "Homestead" is both this South Florida city and the Florida exemption for a primary residence, and the two are not linked automatically. A house in the city must still file for the exemption, and homes anywhere in Miami-Dade can claim it.

sections.h2: When do tax notices arrive and what do early payers save?
sections.html:
Notices are mailed around October 30, with online viewing and payment starting that day. Payment without penalty runs through March 31.

Early payment discounts
Month of paymentDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchGross tax

A check mailed to the Miami address earns the discount by its postmark. Bank bill-pay services need about five business days, so schedule early and quote the folio number printed on the notice.

On April 1 the account is delinquent and takes at least 3% interest plus advertising and fee charges. If 2026 tax is not paid before June 1, 2027, a certificate may be issued, and that year's certificate sale is scheduled to start June 1, 2027.

A certificate can end in loss of the property down the line. The investor holding it may petition for a deed once two full years pass after the April 1 of issue. At the clerk's auction, the winner puts down 5 percent of the bid (or $200 if that is more) and pays the balance and fees within a day.

One local wrinkle: some Miami-Dade bills carry a Water, Road and Sewer assessment collected in 30-year annual installments. That portion must be paid by May 31 or a certificate is sold on the remaining lien balance. Look for the line on your notice.

A qualifying owner can reduce assessed value by up to $50,000 in two slices. School taxes see only the first $25,000, and the second slice applies to value above $50,000. You must live there on January 1, and Form DR-501 is due at the Property Appraiser's office by March 1.

  • The exemption ends if the home is rented out or you stop being a Florida resident.
  • Save Our Homes limits each year's rise in assessed value to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is less. The state's chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • After title changes hands, the next January 1 resets value to just value, with a few spouse and inheritance exceptions.
  • Portability carries some of the capped savings to a new Florida homestead. File DR-501T, and set up the new home within three years of the January 1 after you left the old one.

Buyers can run the Property Appraiser's online tax estimator before making an offer.

sections.h2: What can an owner do about a value or exemption notice?
sections.html:
TRIM notices arrive from the Property Appraiser each August. A petition to the Value Adjustment Board is due 25 days after the mailing, and a denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

Filing the exemption on time avoids the need for an appeal. If a Property Appraiser or board ruling produces a refund, the collector's FAQ has an email address for it. A refund that arises from a sale is a different matter, settled between buyer and seller at closing.

sections.h2: City of Homestead millage and bonds
sections.html:
The city's approved FY 2026 to 2027 budget leaves the operating millage rate where it was the year before. Total millage on any parcel is the sum of every taxing district, so read the rate on your own notice.

On November 4, 2025, the city put two general obligation bonds to voters, one for parks and one for roads. The city's FAQ estimated 0.3661 mills for parks and 0.3983 mills for roadways if all of it were issued, with borrowing in several series. Ask the city whether either bond now shows on your parcel.

sections.h2: Paying the bill and finding older records
sections.html:
The collector takes payment online by check, credit card or debit card. In person it accepts check, cashier's check, money order, certified funds, cash, cards or Apple Pay. By mail, write the folio number and a phone number on a check made out to the Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector in U.S. funds, and leave out sensitive details.

  • Wire payments: email the wire address on the collector's FAQ page for instructions. A wire takes one to two business days to post.
  • Older bills: the collector can supply tax records older than those online, and the FAQ lists an email address for the request.
  • Escrow: if you are unsure whether your lender is paying, ask the lender directly.
  • Roll changes: the certified tax roll reaches the collector once a year, around November 1, so recent ownership or address changes may not show online before then.

Florida has no personal property tax on vehicles, which spares a seller who is also moving a car or boat from one more bill.

sections.h2: Before closing on a Homestead house
sections.html:
Miami-Dade uses its own deed stamp rate: 60 cents per $100 plus a 45-cent surtax, with the surtax skipped on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Most other counties charge 70 cents per $100. Every party to a document can be held liable.

  • Get a written payoff, and ask whether a delinquency or certificate notice exists.
  • Ask the title company how the year will be divided between you and the buyer.
  • Review the clerk's records for liens and check for a Water, Road and Sewer assessment.
  • Report any quarterly installment payments already made, since missing the July 31 first-payment cutoff removes the account from the plan.

Bring the folio number and a copy of your deed when you contact any office. When back taxes or a title problem would stall a buyer who needs a bank loan, a cash purchase lets the title company clear the debt from your proceeds without waiting on lender approval.

faqs.q: Who bills a house in the City of Homestead?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade County Office of the Tax Collector. The city sets a rate but does not send a bill.

faqs.q: When is Homestead real estate tax late?
faqs.a: After March 31. April 1 brings at least 3% interest plus advertising costs and fees.

faqs.q: Does a tax certificate mean the city takes my house?
faqs.a: Not yet. The certificate is a lien an investor buys, and a deed application cannot come until two years after that April 1.

faqs.q: Do I qualify for the exemption if I move in during the spring?
faqs.a: Not for that year. You must live there on January 1 and file by March 1, and a sale resets the buyer's assessed value the next January 1.

faqs.q: Does the City of Homestead add its own transfer tax?
faqs.a: Ask the city whether any local charge applies. The state deed stamp tax applies at the Miami-Dade rate.
